rows.description: I say "then I will not eat" or cry loudly in front of visitors so they say yes. It sometimes works, so I keep doing it. Wise parents stay kind and steady. Rewarding pressure teaches that shouting wins.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, resentment, trust
related mind states: sadness

rows.description: My baby brother cries and I pat him and fetch Mummy. I feel big and needed. A wise parent thanks me but does not make me a permanent little parent, because I am a child too.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, jealousy, neglect
related mind states: gratitude

rows.description: When the baby cries my parent runs to him and I feel forgotten. I may act out to get noticed. A wise parent gives me a small job and a special time each day so I feel seen too.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, jealousy, protectiveness

rows.description: The crying is loud and I cover my ears and want it to stop. This feeling is normal and does not make me bad. A wise action is to walk away or play elsewhere. The harmful pattern is pinching the baby to make him quiet.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, jealousy, neglect, protectiveness
related mind states: sadness, anger

rows.description: Everyone visits the baby and gives gifts and I feel invisible and angry. I may say "send him back". Wise parents accept the feeling, keep my routine and include me. Hitting the baby needs gentle firm stopping.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, affection, neglect
this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: anger, jealousy

rows.description: I stroke the baby's tiny hand and feel amazed and tender. I want to help by bringing a diaper. This early love is real and sometimes mixes with jealousy on the same day. Both feelings can be true.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, jealousy, neglect
this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: affection, jealousy, awe

rows.description: Mummy is tired and busy with the baby and I feel pushed out. I may cling or regress to baby talk. This is not my fault and I am still loved. Ten minutes of undivided attention each day helps me a lot.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, affection, jealousy
this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: affection, tiredness

rows.description: My parent says "you are still my big and little one, and there is room for both of you". I feel secure. Being told my place in the family is safe lets the jealousy soften into pride in being an elder sibling.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, jealousy, neglect
this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3
related mind states: pride, jealousy, trust

rows.description: Dadi hugs me first, not the baby, and says "you are my special one". I feel safe and important again. Relatives who notice the older child during a new-baby time protect them from feeling replaced.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, jealousy, neglect

related mind states: affection, trust

rows.description: My sibling broke my drawing and I hit back. I feel the anger in my whole body. A wise child says "you broke it, I am mad" and gets help. Hitting brings a punishment and my sibling then feels angry too.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: forgiveness, loyalty, rivalry
